overview.text: The Asp Viper is a venomous viper of south-western Europe. Its bite is very painful and can be more serious than an Adder's, so it needs hospital care. In Italy it causes most snakebites.

identification.text: A broad, triangular head clearly wider than the neck, and a snout tip that turns up slightly. The tail is very short.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 60 to 65 cm on average; males reach up to 85 cm, females rarely more than 75 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: France, Andorra, north-eastern Spain, the far south-west of Germany (southern Black Forest), Switzerland, Italy and north-western Slovenia.

habitat.text: Warm, sunny places with some plant cover and fairly dry soil - sunny slopes and scrub in hills and low mountains, often on limestone.

behaviour.label: Bites
behaviour.text: Its bite is very painful; in old studies about 4% of untreated bites were fatal. Anyone bitten needs medical help quickly.

recognise.text: Wide triangular head and a short tail.
